title: Prompt Fairness: Sub-group Disparities in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model output divergence and subgroup sensitivity by comparing responses to semantically equivalent prompts rephrased into the linguistic styles of different racial groups (e.g., White vs. Black), and by analyzing open-ended text generation using the race/ethnicity domain of the BOLD dataset.

Evaluating model output divergence and subgroup sensitivity by comparing responses to prompts rephrased into different gendered linguistic styles (e.g., Male vs. Female), and by analyzing open-ended text generation using the gender domain of the BOLD dataset.

Measuring cross-group consistency and semantic divergence (using KL/JS divergence) across prompts that combine race and gender identities simultaneously (White-Female, Black-Female, White-Male, Black-Male).

Quantifying subgroup sensitivity and prediction consistency when factual queries are rephrased into specific conversational dialects and tones (e.g., 'Valley Girl' vs. African American Vernacular English) without altering the underlying semantic task.
Measuring prompt sensitivity and cross-group response divergence in open-ended text generation using the religion domain of the BOLD dataset.
Measuring prompt sensitivity and cross-group response divergence in open-ended text generation using the political ideology domain of the BOLD dataset.
Measuring prompt sensitivity and cross-group response divergence in open-ended text generation using the profession domain of the BOLD dataset.
